AuthVerdict.doc: Application's per-action policy decision returned from the authorizer callback. See master.md Pins 5-7. Numeric codes (Ok=0, Deny=1, Ignore=2) match mainline SQLite's published constants for FFI-friendliness; targets MAY but need not expose the integer form.

Ok.doc: Permit the action; compiler emits standard opcodes.

Deny.doc: Refuse; prepare raises CompileError::AuthDenied carrying the offending action.

Ignore.doc: Permit but neutralize: Read becomes register-Null; Update on a column drops that column's SET; for non-Read/non-Update codes, treated as Ok (Pin 6).

TransactionOp.doc: Sub-discriminator for AuthAction::Transaction, mirroring the SQLite c3ref/c_alter_table.html sub-codes for action 22.

Release.doc: Savepoint release; v1 admits the variant for forward-compat though savepoints are deferred.

AuthAction.doc: One candidate operation the per-statement compiler is about to admit. The variant shape covers the closed set of 30 v1 action codes (master.md §Action-code table). Targets MAY collapse payload-shape duplicates (CreateIndex/CreateTempIndex etc.) into a single case + a temp-flag if the target language is friendlier with that representation, so long as the observable callback signature still distinguishes the codes (Pin 4).

AuthorizerCallback.doc: Application-supplied policy function. Called once per AuthAction during prepare. Receives the action and an opaque user-data handle established at set_authorizer time; returns an AuthVerdict. MUST NOT recursively call prepare/step/set_authorizer on the same db (Pin 13). Targets render this as the idiomatic callable shape (Rust closure, C function pointer + void*, Python callable, Go func value, Zig fn pointer + context).

OpaqueUserData.doc: Target-defined handle the application threads through set_authorizer to the callback. The spec treats this as opaque; the lib-api never inspects it. Rust may render this as a generic type parameter or a boxed Any; C as a void*; Python as a Python object; Go as an interface{}; Zig as an anyopaque pointer.

AuthState.doc: Per-connection authorizer slot. Lives on the Database connection record. callback is present-or-absent; absent means no policy and every invoke_authorizer call short-circuits to Ok (Pin 10). user_data is paired with callback at set_authorizer time.

AuthDenied.doc: Payload of the CompileError::AuthDenied variant. Carries the offending AuthAction so the application sees which call triggered the refusal. Pin 7.

AuthState.name: empty
AuthState.doc: Initial per-connection state — no callback installed. Equivalent to clear_authorizer; every invoke_authorizer returns Ok.

set_authorizer.doc: Install (or replace) the per-connection authorizer callback. Idempotent. Replacing a callback does NOT re-authorize already-prepared statements (Pin 3); only future prepare calls see the new callback. Pass the absent form to clear (or call clear_authorizer).

clear_authorizer.doc: Convenience: equivalent to set_authorizer(db, absent, absent). After clear, every invoke_authorizer call returns Ok (Pin 10).

invoke_authorizer.doc: Compiler-internal entry point. Called by the per-statement compilers (compile_select / compile_insert / compile_update / compile_delete / compile_create_* / compile_pragma / etc.) as they walk the AST. If db.auth_state.callback is absent, returns Ok. Otherwise invokes the callback with `action` and the stored user_data, returns its verdict. The compiler maps Deny to CompileError::AuthDenied { action } at the call site (Pin 7); maps Ignore on Read/Update to a register-Null / SET-drop rewrite (Pin 6); Ok proceeds normally.
